cards.name: phase_gradient_catalysis_dyadic_rotations
cards.identity: Allocate an m-qubit CLEAN ancilla register G (m = 9 here) and prepare the phase-gradient catalyst |grad_m> = 2^(-m/2) * sum_{y=0}^{2^m-1} e^{2*pi*i*y/2^m} |y>, which factorizes as a product state tensor_{b=0}^{m-1} (|0> + e^{2*pi*i*2^b/2^m}|1>)/sqrt(2); so prep = H on each G qubit followed by rz(2*pi*2^b/2^m) on qubit b (b = m-1,m-2,m-3 are Z, S, T: EXACT and free; only b <= m-4, i.e. angles pi/8 ... 2*pi/2^m, need gridsynth, ONCE). Let ADD_c be addition of the integer constant c mod 2^m into G. Because |grad_m> is an eigenstate of ADD_c with eigenvalue e^(-2*pi*i*c/2^m), a controlled-ADD_c with control qubit q applies the single-qubit diagonal phase diag(1, e^(-2*pi*i*c/2^m)) on q and leaves G untouched: a controlled-rotation implemented by classical reversible arithmetic, i.e. ANDs (Toffolis), with NO rotation synthesis. More generally, controlled addition of a w-bit QUANTUM register X (control q) applies phase e^(-2*pi*i*q*X/2^m), which is one gate fusing an entire QFT stage's worth of rotations. Procedure: (1) rewrite every rz in the circuit as (exact Clifford+T multiple of pi/4) * (residual +-2*pi*c/2^m); (2) emit the pi/4 part exactly; (3) replace each residual by the corresponding controlled addition into G, fusing, inside each Hadamard-free segment, all residual rotations that share a control qubit q and whose remaining support is a register X into a SINGLE controlled-add of X (shifted) into G; (4) implement every addition with Gidney measurement-uncomputed AND gadgets (4 T per AND, temporary ancillas returned by measurement); (5) at the end, G is returned EXACTLY in the product state |grad_m>, unentangled from the data, so each G qubit is measured in the X basis and reset to |0> by a classically controlled X -- the catalyst uncompute costs 0 T.
cards.correctness: ADD_c|y> = |y + c mod 2^m>, so ADD_c|grad_m> = 2^(-m/2) sum_y e^(2*pi*i*y/2^m)|y+c> = 2^(-m/2) sum_{y'} e^(2*pi*i*(y'-c)/2^m)|y'> = e^(-2*pi*i*c/2^m)|grad_m>: the catalyst is an exact eigenvector (phase kickback, Kitaev-Shen-Vyalyi). Hence control-ADD_c acts as |q>|grad> -> e^(-2*pi*i*c*q/2^m)|q>|grad>, i.e. exactly diag(1, e^(-2*pi*i*c/2^m)) on q tensor identity on G -- a Z-rotation up to a global phase and a recorded Clifford phase. Linearity extends this to a controlled add of a quantum addend X: phase e^(-2*pi*i*q*X/2^m), the exact diagonal phase polynomial of a fused QFT stage. The additions themselves are classical reversible permutations, verified exactly; the AND gadgets with measured uncompute satisfy the relaxed contract (clean ancillas restored to |0>, each measurement branch applies the same function with a branch phase c_m fixed by the classically controlled CZ fix-up, independent of x). G stays unentangled and exactly restored, so measuring it in the X basis at the end cannot disturb the data register; the classically controlled X returns it to |0>. The ONLY approximation is the one-time catalyst preparation: synthesizing the m-3 non-Clifford gradient rotations to accuracy delta each gives total state error <= sum delta, and since the catalyst is reused R times the induced circuit distance is <= R * sum_b delta_b; choose delta_b = 5e-4/(R*(m-3)) (R <= 21 here, so delta ~ 2.6e-6, about 60-70 T per rotation) and charge that single bound to the approx half of the ledger. All 48 original rotations then disappear at ZERO approximation cost.
cards.trigger: Clifford+Rz op list in which, for every rz with a non-multiple-of-pi/4 angle theta, reducing theta mod 2*pi and subtracting the nearest multiple of pi/4 leaves a residual r with |r * 2^m/(2*pi) - round(r * 2^m/(2*pi))| < 1e-9 for some m <= 12 (i.e. all residuals are dyadic multiples of 2*pi). On qft_8 this holds for ALL 48 rz: the 42 angles +-pi/8, +-pi/16, +-pi/32, +-pi/64, +-pi/128, +-pi/256 (the CRz(pi/2^(k-1)) pairs of the textbook QFT, k = 3..8) and the 6 angles 1.178097, 1.374447, 1.472622, 1.521709, 1.546253, 7.84171, each of which is pi/2 (or 5*pi/2) minus one of pi/8, pi/16, pi/32, pi/64, pi/128, pi/256, i.e. Clifford * dyadic. Fire only if the number of such rz is >= 8 (so one catalyst prep is amortized), and take m = max over residuals of the required dyadic depth (m = 9 here). Fusion sub-trigger: within a Hadamard-free segment, residual rotations whose Pauli-frame parity labels (as computed by the existing pauli_frame pass) all contain a common qubit q and differ only in the other wires are merged into one controlled add of that register into G.
cards.expected_effect: All 48 gridsynth-synthesized rotations (essentially all 1568 of the current 1583 T; only the 15 explicit t/tdg are not from synthesis) are replaced by additions into the catalyst. Per-stage fusion gives 7 controlled additions of a w-bit addend (w = 1..7) into the 9-bit G; a Gidney controlled ripple-carry add of a w-bit addend with carry propagation to the top of G costs about (9 + w) measurement-uncomputed ANDs, i.e. 4*(9+w) T: sum over w = 1..7 gives about 4 * 91 = 364 T, plus a handful of CZ/CX fix-ups (0 T). One-time catalyst prep: m - 3 = 6 non-Clifford gradient rotations at delta ~ 2.6e-6, about 65 T each = ~390 T (Z, S, T on the three most significant gradient qubits are exact and free), and the catalyst uncompute is free (X-basis measurement + classical X). Total new T ~ 364 + 390 + 15 = ~770, against 1583 now, 1577 for pyzx and 2391 for TKET / BQSKit-FT. Cost is +9 clean ancilla qubits (8 -> 17, plus 1-2 transient AND ancillas) and a shift of the non-Clifford content from rotation synthesis (which scales as 48 * 3*log2(1/eps_rz)) to arithmetic (which scales as O(n^2) ANDs, precision-independent), so the margin grows at smaller eps.
cards.source: Phase-gradient / catalyst phase kickback: Kitaev, Shen, Vyalyi, 'Classical and Quantum Computation' (2002), phase estimation kickback; C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018), arXiv:1709.06648 (measurement-uncomputed AND, 4 T, and the phase-gradient register); C. Gidney and M. Ekera, 'How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers in 8 hours', Quantum 5, 433 (2021), Appendix on phase-gradient rotations (controlled addition into a gradient register as a controlled Z-rotation, catalyst reused across all rotations); D. Coppersmith, 'An approximate Fourier transform useful in quantum factoring', IBM RC19642 (1994), for the dyadic rotation structure of the QFT.

cards.name: multilinear_phase_polynomial_and_ancilla_resynthesis
cards.identity: Per Hadamard-free segment, put the segment in phase-polynomial normal form D . L (Amy-Maslov-Mosca): L = the segment's linear/Clifford part (cx, cz, x, z, s), D = a diagonal phase on the segment INPUT variables x_1..x_n, obtained by pulling every rotation backwards through the cx network (each rotation's wire carries a known GF(2) parity label p = XOR_{i in S} x_i, exactly the label the existing pauli_frame pass already computes). D(x) = exp(i * sum_j c_j * p_j(x)) with c_j the rotation angles (t = pi/4, tdg = -pi/4, rz(a) = a, sign per rz convention). Now change basis from GF(2) parities to ARITHMETIC multilinear monomials using (-1)^p = prod_{i in S}(1 - 2 x_i), i.e. p = 1/2 - 1/2 * prod_{i in S}(1 - 2 x_i) = 1/2 - 1/2 * sum_{T subset S} (-2)^{|T|} prod_{i in T} x_i. Collect coefficients: D(x) = exp(i * (const + sum_T alpha_T prod_{i in T} x_i)), alpha_T = -(1/2) * sum_{j : T subset S_j} c_j * (-2)^{|T|}, reduced mod 2*pi; the constant is a true global phase and is dropped. Emit D monomial by monomial (all monomials are diagonal, hence mutually commuting, so any order works): |T| = 1 -> a single rz(alpha_T) on wire i (synthesized by gridsynth only if alpha_T is not a multiple of pi/4); |T| = 2, T = {i,k} -> allocate ONE clean ancilla a, a = x_i AND x_k with Gidney's measurement-uncomputed AND gadget (4 T to compute, 0 T to uncompute: measure a in the X basis and apply a classically controlled CZ(x_i,x_k) fix-up), apply rz(alpha_T) on a, then uncompute; |T| >= 3 -> left-associated chain of the same AND gadget (|T| - 1 ANDs). The single ancilla is reused because the monomials are emitted sequentially. Then emit L unchanged. Fire only when this strictly reduces the number of gridsynth-synthesized rotations by more than the AND overhead pays back (see trigger).
cards.correctness: Two exact facts. (1) Normal form: cx/x conjugation maps a Z-rotation about parity p to a Z-rotation about the pulled-back parity (Z_q -> Z_{L^{-1} q}), and all Z-rotations in a Hadamard-free, cx/x/diagonal segment commute with each other, so moving every rotation to the segment start is an exact identity up to global phase; the resulting operator is diagonal in the computational basis with eigenvalue exp(i sum_j c_j p_j(x)) on |x>. (2) Basis change: for x_i in {0,1}, 1 - 2 x_i = (-1)^{x_i}, hence prod_{i in S}(1-2x_i) = (-1)^{XOR_{i in S} x_i}, so p = (1 - (-1)^p)/2 is EXACTLY the stated multilinear polynomial on the Boolean cube; expanding the product and collecting gives alpha_T as an identity over the reals, not an approximation. Therefore sum_j c_j p_j(x) = const + sum_T alpha_T prod_{i in T} x_i for every x, and the two emissions are the same diagonal unitary up to global phase. Implementing a monomial: with a = prod_{i in T} x_i in a clean ancilla, rz(alpha_T) on a contributes diag(e^{-i alpha_T/2}, e^{+i alpha_T/2}) = e^{-i alpha_T/2} * e^{i alpha_T a}, i.e. the wanted phase times a constant (x-independent) global factor. Gidney's AND gadget computes a = x_i AND x_k exactly on a |0> ancilla with 4 T, and its measurement-based uncompute returns the ancilla to |0> with a classically controlled Clifford fix-up; in each measurement branch the same function is applied with the same branch phase c_m for all x (phase consistency), and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1, so the relaxed-contract spec check passes. Approximation enters ONLY through gridsynth on the surviving rz, now at eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz' with the smaller N_Rz', so the ledger bound strictly improves.
cards.trigger: A Clifford+Rz op list. Partition into maximal segments containing no h (ops h delimit; cx, cz, x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz are inside). For each segment: track the affine parity label of every wire from the segment inputs (pauli_frame machinery), read off the multiset {(c_j, S_j)} of rotation angles and their parity supports, build the monomial coefficients alpha_T as above (reduce mod 2*pi, drop |alpha_T| < 1e-12), and let R_old = #{j : c_j not a multiple of pi/4} (rotations that cost gridsynth) and R_new = #{T : alpha_T not a multiple of pi/4}, A = sum over those T of (|T| - 1) ANDs. Rewrite the segment only if 32 * (R_old - R_new) > 4 * A + 8, i.e. the removed synthesis strictly dominates the AND cost (the 32 is the measured gridsynth T-cost at this eps; the implementer should use the api's cost model if available). Monomials whose alpha_T IS a multiple of pi/4 are emitted as Clifford/T on the AND ancilla only if that is cheaper than leaving the contributing rotations alone; otherwise the segment's pi/4-multiple content is emitted directly as Clifford+T with no ancilla. On qft_8 this fires on every stage segment: stage j (after h on qubit j) carries the controlled-phase rotations between qubit j and qubits j+1..7, which TKET has left as about 2 synthesized rz per controlled-phase on parities x_j and x_j XOR x_k, while the arithmetic form has exactly ONE quadratic monomial x_j x_k per controlled-phase and NO linear terms (the linear parts of the two parities cancel: c*(x_j) + c*(x_k) - c*(x_j XOR x_k) = 2c*x_j*x_k).
cards.expected_effect: qft_8's full phase polynomial is sum_{i<j} (pi/2^{j-i}) x_i x_j: exactly 21 quadratic monomials with non-pi/4 angles (the 21 pairs at distance >= 2) plus 7 monomials with alpha = pi/2 at distance 1 (Clifford, emitted as the existing s/t content, left alone). The 48 synthesized rz collapse to 21 synthesized rz, one per monomial, each on a single AND ancilla: 27 gridsynth rotations disappear. Each quadratic monomial needs 1 AND (4 T compute, 0 T measured uncompute) = 84 T total, and the ANDs are sequential so ONE clean ancilla suffices (8 -> 9 qubits, lexicographically after T-count). Re-budgeting: N_Rz falls 48 -> 21, so eps_rz rises from 2.08e-5 to 4.8e-5 and each surviving rotation costs about 29-31 T instead of 32.7. New T ~= 21 * 30 + 84 + 15 (the existing t/tdg from the distance-1 controlled-phases) ~= 730, against 1583 now, 1577 for pyzx, 2029 for BQSKit-DPF and 2391 for TKET / BQSKit-FT. The saving is structural (parity basis -> monomial basis is where the QFT is sparse) and grows at smaller eps, since it trades 27 precision-dependent synthesis costs for 21 precision-independent ANDs. Unlike pure rotation merging, no two rotations need to share a parity label, so nothing depends on Hadamards being crossable: every monomial lives inside the single stage segment that created it.
cards.source: Phase-polynomial normal form for Hadamard-free segments: M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits via matroid partitioning' (2014). Parity-to-monomial (Fourier/Reed-Muller) change of basis for diagonal unitaries: J. Welch, D. Greenbaum, S. Kimmel, A. Aspuru-Guzik, 'Efficient quantum circuits for diagonal unitaries without ancillas' (2014). AND gadget with measurement-based uncompute (4 T, clean ancilla): C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition' (2018); phases applied to AND ancillas as in Gidney & Fowler, 'Flexible layout of surface code computations' (2019) and the Hamming-weight-phasing construction of Kivlichan et al. (2020).

New T ~= 21 * 30 + 84 + 15 (the existing t/tdg from the distance-1 controlled-phases) ~= 730, against 1583 now, 1577 for pyzx, 2029 for BQSKit-DPF and 2391 for TKET / BQSKit-FT. The saving is structural (parity basis -> monomial basis is where the QFT is sparse) and grows at smaller eps, since it trades 27 precision-dependent synthesis costs for 21 precision-independent ANDs. Unlike pure rotation merging, no two rotations need to share a parity label, so nothing depends on Hadamards being crossable: every monomial lives inside the single stage segment that created it.
